text:
A: Hi, erm, can you hear me okay?
B: Yes, I can hear you. Hi. I'm Aneesa.
A: I'm Rayhan. Nice to meet you. Where are you calling from?
B: Bradford. You?
A: Ilford, East London. Erm. Did you find that puzzle at the start alright?
B: It was fine. I was more interested in why they put it first, to be honest. I think it's to put everyone in the same sort of mood before the calls. Or tired. One of the two.
A: Ha, yeah, I was tired after it. I'd just got in from work as well.
B: What do you do?
A: I'm an apprentice electrician, final year. Small firm in Barking, mostly houses: rewires, kitchens, bit of shop fit-out. I've got my AM2 coming up, that's like the final practical assessment, so I'm a bit... yeah. Revising for that.
B: That sounds quite intense. Is it all practical?
A: Mostly. You get a set time to install and test a little setup in a booth, and they mark everything. You can't really rush it. If you mess up the testing you're done, basically. I test twice anyway, the lads on site wind me up for it.
B: Twice seems sensible when it's electricity.
A: That's what I say! Erm, what about you, what do you do?
B: I'm doing a psychology degree with the Open University, second year. And I work part-time in a fragrance shop in town, Saturdays mainly.
A: Oh, nice. So is this sort of your area, then, these studies?
B: Kind of. I do a few of them. Partly for the money, I won't lie. But I like seeing how they're set up, what they're actually measuring. Like the photo bit earlier, rating people on a picture, that's a first impressions thing. Then they'll compare it with what we say after.
A: Oh. I didn't really think about that. I just sort of went with my gut.
B: That's what they want, I think. It's fine.
A: Yeah. Your photo, the planner on the wall, it reminded me of my sister. She's doing her GCSEs, she's got colours for every subject.
B: Guilty. Mine's colour-coded too. I've got a sister who's fourteen. She just borrows my eyeliner and ignores the planner entirely.
A: Ha. Mine's alright, she asks me for maths help. I got a 7 in maths so I'm the go-to.
B: That's useful. Do you get much time, with the work and revising?
A: Not loads. I do football Thursday, gym some mornings. Weekends is mostly family stuff, weddings. There's always a wedding.
B: There's always a wedding. Same here.
A: Have you been anywhere nice, travelling? I went to Istanbul last summer with two mates, first time without family.
B: Istanbul? That's the one place I really want to go. I'm learning Turkish on Duolingo, I've got a streak of four hundred and something days. Was it good?
A: It was really good, yeah. The mosques, like the Blue Mosque and Süleymaniye, the architecture is unbelievable. And the food. I did the whole itinerary in a spreadsheet, my mates took the mick but we saw everything.
B: You did a spreadsheet? I did that for Barcelona with my cousins. Every hour planned. They complained the whole time and then thanked me after.
A: Same! That's exactly what happened. Would you use the Turkish, if you went?
B: I'd try. I can order tea and ask where the toilet is, so I'd survive. I'd mostly want to sit in Süleymaniye and draw the tiles. I do geometric patterns, ink drawings.
A: Oh, is that the one behind you? The star?
B: Yeah, that's one of mine.
A: That's really neat. Like, properly precise. I'd mess that up.
B: You'd probably be fine. You test everything twice.
